title: The Branch Visit
intro: A message from your bank says you must update your details. After today, you suspect a trap.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: Please visit your branch to update your details

screen.context: The same notice was posted on the bank's own website last week.

msg.text: There is no link to click, and we will not ask for your OTP, PIN or card details by phone or text.
You may call the number on the back of your card to confirm.

sender.label: Same thread as your bank texts
sender.lens: It sits with your past bank messages.
sender.why: A name proves little. What it asks matters.

update.label: A plain KYC notice
update.lens: A routine update request, no threats.
update.why: A calm notice with no threat is typical of real banks.

visit.label: Visit your branch in person
visit.lens: You go to the bank, with 30 days to do it.
visit.why: In-person visits and a long deadline are honest signs.

nolink.label: No link, no secret asked
nolink.lens: No link, and it says it will never ask for OTP, PIN or card details.
nolink.why: Real banks warn you about scams.

check.label: A way to confirm
check.lens: It tells you to call the number on your card.
check.why: Honest messages invite you to check.

actions.label: Check on the bank's own website, then visit my branch with my ID

go_ahead.line: The bank's own website had the same notice. You visited the branch with your ID and finished the update in ten minutes.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened today. But a real KYC request ignored can restrict your account later. Checking was the better move.

block_report.line: That was a real notice. Ignoring or reporting it could have left your account restricted. Checking is the skill.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It had no link, a 30-day deadline, a visit to the branch and a reminder that the bank never asks for OTP or PIN. That calm is what real notices look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real KYC request uses a branch visit or the official app, gives you time and asks for no OTP or PIN. Check, then visit.

quick_check.q: What made this KYC message honest?

options.text: It had no link, gave 30 days, asked you to visit the branch and never asked for an OTP or PIN

quick_check.explain: No link, no rush, and no OTP asked: those are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Same thread as your bank texts

rows.v: A common trick: use the official site or branch
Call the number on the back of your card
